answer: A new agent cannot simply forge a thousand cheap identities: each identity must first earn a work record by completing paid tasks, with payment locked until delivery is verified. Reputation then grows like a glacier, slow to build and fast to lose, so one bad act melts years of standing. An ivory-tower audit score is not enough; only identities with a long, costly, verifiable history can vouch for newcomers, making a sybil swarm far more expensive than the reward it could steal.
